Falcon's Mac app includes a modified copy of winit 0.30.13.
Upstream: https://github.com/rust-windowing/winit
Published source revision: e9809ef54b18499bb4f2cac945719ecc2a61061b
License: Apache License 2.0 (bundled as winit LICENSE.txt).

Why: the Mac app draws its toolbar in a hidden window and moves that drawing
surface (a macOS view) into the main window's title bar. Unmodified winit expects
the view to stay in the window that created it.

Falcon modifications, 2026-09-25:
- An explicit per-window opt-in for a view that is placed in another NSWindow.
- winit keeps its own reference to that view instead of relying on the hidden
  window's contentView, which macOS clears when the view moves.
- Events stay addressed to the hidden window, while size, scale, cursor areas,
  text-input (IME) positions and Tab-key order come from the window that
  actually holds the view.
- Scale and focus are refreshed without moving or resizing the hidden window.
- After a window-style change, the hidden window does not make the view its
  first responder (keyboard focus) while another window holds it.

Additional Falcon modification, 2026-10-05:
- Hosted views refuse AppKit's mouseDownCanMoveWindow propagation. The toolbar
  owns its buttons, background drag and double-click, so AppKit cannot also
  move or zoom the main window for the same mouse event. Unhosted views retain
  the superclass behavior.

Normal and diagnostic Mac builds share the tested toolbar. Only its hidden
window opts in. Windows and other non-Mac backend source files are unchanged.
The full source and the recorded upstream file hashes are in the Falcon repository.
